anchors: A lax-mode model field is not a check on numeric or date TEXT
decision: A lax-mode Pydantic field is not boundary validation for numeric or date text; check the raw string (before-validator with length bound and [0-9] fullmatch) or use a constrained str field, and pin the accepted oddities as refusal tests.

evidence.text: pydantic 2.14.3: int accepts '1_0', '+2', ' 7 ', leading zeros; Decimal accepts '1e3' and Arabic-Indic digits; date accepts a midnight datetime with offset; int refuses Arabic-Indic digits.

reopen_if: Pydantic's lax mode stops accepting these strings.
why: A lax int/Decimal/date field accepts underscores, signs, padding, exponents, non-ASCII digits and datetime strings that a sibling [0-9] parser refuses, so two boundaries disagree.

decision: An upper-case-only rule is written per character, refusing a character only when its upper case is one character and differs from it; sharp s and the U+FB0x ligatures sit on the accept side of the test.

evidence.text: Python: chr(0xDF).upper() == 'SS'; U+FB00-U+FB06 upper-case to 2-3 letters.

reopen_if: Unicode changes the full upper-case mapping of U+00DF and the ligatures.
why: s == s.upper() can never hold for characters whose upper case is longer, so valid identifiers are refused.
